Lessons.Title: Solve Multiplicative Comparison Problems
ExplanationParagraphs:
Learning goal: You will interpret and represent multiplicative comparison situations in which a factor is unknown.
In previous lessons, you matched descriptions, equations, and discrete diagrams that represented multiplicative comparison.
Core relationship: Unknown factors in multiplicative comparisons. Write total = multiplier × base; divide the total by multiplier when base is missing.

Local publisher 2021 source lesson activities: Warm-up:  Number Talk: Find the Unknown Factor	 (10 minutes); Activity 1:  A Book Drive	 (20 minutes); Activity 2:  Represent a Missing Amount	 (15 minutes); Cool-down:  Back at the Book Drive	 (5 minutes)
Source-aligned Edulytics model: Seven times a number is 56. Find the number.
First-party Cool-down (not gated original): A book drive raises 6 times as many books as a starting set of 9. What is the total?
Original visual/physical and peer-explanation activities still require teacher review.

KeyConcepts.Title: Unknown factors in multiplicative comparisons
KeyConcepts.Rule: Write total = multiplier × base; divide the total by multiplier when base is missing.
KeyConcepts.Example: Seven times a number is 56. Find the number.

KeyConcepts.Title: Mathematical relationship
KeyConcepts.Definition: Unknown comparison factors can be found by division.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Unknown comparison factors can be found by division.
KeyConcepts.Example: One collection has 9 objects and another 36. How many times as many?

KeyConcepts.Title: Exact inverse and unit check
KeyConcepts.Example: A ribbon is 45 cm long, five times another ribbon. Find the shorter ribbon.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Subtracting multiplier from total rather than dividing to find the unit group.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: It changes the unit, place value, or operation.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Write total = multiplier × base; divide the total by multiplier when base is missing.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Treating 36 compared with 9 as 36−9 times as many.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The comparison ratio or measurement units do not match the task.
